Alexandra Renewal Project - the aftermath

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
While authorities labour on investigations, the Alexandra community looks to a future where residents make the most of the little they have to move the township forward.

Unique Selling Point:
The highlight of this insert is getting an inside look at the status of the City of Johannesburg's investigation into the missing Alexandra Renewal Project millions – the investigation has not even begun! The city is swamped with thousands of documents which still need to be categorised and filed before their contents can be scrutinised for the answers – and we get to see the room with endless stacks of files and documents.

Summary:
We tackle the failures of the Alexandra Renewal Project, specifically the lack of monitoring and accountability that led to the most of R1.6 billion literally going down the drain. And while authorities labour on investigations that are likely to last as long as years, an independent town planner speaks of what would need to happen to upgrade Alexandra going forward. We speak to community members who acknowledge their challenges but also believe that together, the community has a lot to contribute in solving those challenges.

Further information:
- There are several investigations currently looking at the failures of the Alexandra Renewal Project, many still in their infancy.
- The SAHRC is also hoping to unearth the truth about why the project failed and how that has impacted on the human rights of the residents of Alexandra.
- The insert seeks to hold authorities accountable for ARP failures but also to paint a picture of what the future looks like for hopeless residents.

Press Release:


Alex’s Missing Millions
Amid recurring Alex ‘total shutdown’ protests, the community of Alexandra has become a political football that saw many promises being made during the recent elections. Carte Blanche gets a unique behind-the-scenes insight into preparations by the City of Johannesburg’s Forensic Investigation Service to uncover what really happened to the missing millions of the Alexandra Renewal Project, budgeted at R1.3 billion over seven years.
Producer: Ntokozo Miya
Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


ALEXANDRA RENEWAL PROJECT – THE AFTERMATH – final

AUDIO
VO – Sandton – a world-renowned economic hub where the homes are lavish and service delivery almost always runs smoothly. And that is a lot more than one can say about the township on the other side.
LINK - Just across the highway from Africa's richest square mile lies Alexandra, a community that feels forgotten by authorities who once serenaded them with promises of a better life.
VO – In 2001, government launched the Alexandra Renewal Project (ARP) which aimed to spend around R1.3 billion to fix the roads, install sanitation infrastructure and provide housing. The project ran over budget and as much as R1.6 billion was fueled into it.

But the project was plagued by allegations of corruption and financial mismanagement.

Eighteen years later, while authorities scramble to trace the money, residents continue to struggle with poor sanitation and inadequate housing.

Alex FM journalist Ramatamo Sehoai is familiar with the plight of residents following the failure of the ARP.
RAMATAMO SEHOAI – ALEX FM JOURNALIST

Amongst young people, all they are looking up to is to find employment opportunities. But for older people who have been waiting in the queue for houses for a very long time, basically they think politicians are just playing games with them. There are quite a lot of incomplete infrastructure projects for more of this because all of a sudden, the money went missing.
VO – Residents complain that not much has changed since the ARP was launched, and finally, authorities are investigating how the money was spent.
LINK - The Johannesburg municipality hopes that somewhere in these files lies the answer to one of the city's biggest financial mysteries – the missing ARP millions.
VO – The head of the municipality's forensic unit, General Shadrack Sibiya, is tasked with following the ARP money trail.

With his team on hand to ensure that we do not view the contents of the files, Sibiya gave us an exclusive look insde a high-security evidence room.
GEN. SHADRACK SIBIYA – CITY OF JOHANNESBURG

These documents, we seized them from the basement of the ARP project office in Sandton, 800 000 documents that we have to read through. It's something like 3 months now since we started and I think between a year to one year and six months, we should be fine.

MASA – So in about a year and a year and a half, we will know who to blame for what has gone wrong with this project?

SIBIYA – I think so.
VO – The city's ARP probe is so important that evidence must be kept under lock and key. Our team was granted access under very strict conditions.

Mayor Herman Mashaba has asked investigators to lay charges against an official for “unlawfully accessing the city's office” and removing evidence files. The files have since been returned, but it's not clear why the official took them in the first place.
HERMAN MASHABA – JOHANNESBURG MAYOR

It's not just the documents and investigating team that are at risk – our whistleblowers from Alexandra too. I would really appeal to our law enforcement agencies to treat this matter seriously and ensure that everyone is protected in the process.
LINK - Nearly two decades later, Alexandra doesn't look like a township 02:26:08:11 – on which R1.6 billion was spent for upgrades, so where did the money go?
VO – Some of the ARP's plans were initiated but many were left incomplete, including a recreation facility, pedestrian bridges and several hostels.

Actually, more than R1.6 billion have been spent on Alexandra, says Gauteng Human Settlements MEC Lebogang Maile.
LEBOGANG MAILE – GAUTENG HUMAN SETTLEMENTS MEC

I can tell you with certainty that between the provincial government and the municipality, we've spent close to R2 billion.

MASA - To say that R2 billion was spent, that's where we going into how much has been done and is it enough...

MAILE – To ask me whether indeed R2 billion was spent or not, I mean, how should I know? I'm not a quantity surveyor or engineer.
VO – Maile says his department will soon unveil its plans for the future of Alex. The MEC welcomes the ARP investigatioons.

Even with his investigation in its infancy, Sibiya testified at the South African Human Rights Commission, which is also scrutinizing the ARP.
GEN. SHADRACK SIBIYA – CITY OF JOHANNESBURG

SIBIYA – I am not at liberty to repeat what I said there since it was an in-committee. However, as far as I'm concerned, the manner in which this investigation is being conducted. I don't think is the best way we could do it. If we have different types of investigations being conducted on the same project and the same issue, you are going to have many reports being produced that contradict each other.
VO – UJ Town and Regional Planning lecturer Zenzile Mbinza was part of the team that reviewed the impact of the ARP.
ZENZILE MBINZA – UJ TOWN AND REGIONAL PLANNING LECTURER

By the time we did the study there were about between 250- and 300 thousand people there. The infrastructure in Alex is overloaded whether it be sewers, the water and the roads. The uplifting of Alex, from an architect or an aesthetics perspective, also has to be followed in suit by infrastructure development.

MASA – What would it cost for such a project?

ZENZILE - The Alex Renewal Project was budgeted at R1.3 billion. Even that wasn't enough at the time. If you were to factor in inflation and all of those things, now probably it's running into the R2.5 billions.
VO – The shortage of vacant land in Alex is a huge concern.
ZENZILE MBINZA – UJ TOWN AND REGIONAL PLANNING LECTURER

Fundamentally, some people in Alex would have to move but the question is – where would they move to?
VO - Nosisa Mzayiya's home was among those recently demolished for being illegally built on municipal land.
NOSIPHO MZAYIYA – ALEXANDRA RESIDENT

My house was over there where the mattress is along with everything else. I couldn't take anything out of my house including ID's and birth certificates for the kids.
VO – She has taken shelter with neighbours but plans to rebuild her home right here.
NOSIPHO MZAYIYA – ALEXANDRA RESIDENT

The people who are building here are scared that the demolishers might return. They are taking chances because they don't have anywhere else to go.
VO – Mashaba says he has a plan to counter the space problem.
HERMAN MASHABA – JOHANNESBURG MAYOR

We have got properties in the inner city that are hijacked but belong to us as a city of Johannesburg. Insteads of building RDP houses 50, 60 kilometres away from opportunities, we can have RDP houses in the inner city. I don't understand this RDP system. It's actually promoting the apartheid special planning to even another level.
VO – Until the money is accounted for and government finds sustainable solutions for Alex, residents continue to defy the odds. Amid hardships prominent community members are determined to showcase the township's lively spirit.

Every winter, the grounds behind the Madala Hostel host the Maimane Alfred Phiri Games, named after the Alexandra-born soccer legend who founded the event.
UPSOUND FROM GAMES
VO – Down the road at the Alexsan Kopano centre, actor Pule Hlatshwayo works extensively with the youth through his drama workshops.
PULE HLATSHWAYO – ABAKHEMU DRAMA GROUP

It's almost as if there is a threshold for how far one can succeed up to a certain point. We are aiming to push back those boundaries.
VO – Limited funds and resources have not disheartened these stars in the making.
PULE HLATSHWAYO – ABAKHEMU DRAMA GROUP

I did a play called Mshuko with the youth in the township and it was nominated in the Shashalaza Awards for best director and best newcomer.
VO – Through the arts, Pule wants to direct the narrative away from the problems facing the township and instead, towards highlighting Alexandra's up-and-coming screen legends.

PROMOS

What happened to over a billion rands invested in the Alexandra Renewal Project. The city of Joburg tries to solve one of its biggest financial mysteries.

Authorities hope that somewhere among these documents lies the answer to what happened to over a billion rands meant for Alexandra upgrades.

Over a billion rands of taxpayers' money was fueled into the Alexandra Renewal Project but little has changed in the township. Where did the money go?
